summary: Globes reports that Israeli office rents have held firm despite the Israel-Hamas war, even though office supply is large and demand was already soft. Brokers and developers describe renewed interest after a roughly month-long stoppage, mostly in small and medium deals, while major landlords like Azrieli and Amot report no material impact so far. Experts say owners learned from Covid not to cut rents, though sublessors and some purchase-group buildings face pressure.
one_line: Despite oversupply and the Israel-Hamas war, Israeli office rents have barely fallen, with demand recovering mainly in small and medium deals.
key_facts: Less than a month before the war, AI21 Labs, Amnon Shashua's unicorn, announced it was leasing 7,000 square meters for NIS 15 million annually in Tel Aviv's Da Vinci project.
Azrieli Group has 15 office buildings comprising 632,000 square meters with 97% occupancy, and said its Q3 2023 results were not impacted by the war.

Amot Investments has 1.15 million square meters of office space for leasing with 93.5% occupancy and six projects under construction; in Q3 it signed contracts for 14,000 square meters at unchanged rent.

Amot's management estimates that if the war stays on the southern front and lasts no more than two to three months, the effect on the company is not material; a long war or a northern front would cause wider damage.
According to the Central Bureau of Statistics, construction began on 3.56 million square meters of office space between 2020 and 2022.
Avison Young Israel co-CEO Guy Amosi says office prices have fallen by about 10% at most, and cuts are mainly in buildings sold to purchase groups such as BSR City.
Amosi said a company seeking 15,000 square meters avoided Tel Aviv, where contracts were closed two years ago at NIS 150 per square meter, and looked between Rishon Lezion and Kfar Saba.

Natalie Marshall of Marshall Strategic Real Estate said office marketing stopped for a month but movement recommenced about two weeks before the article, with companies searching for 10,000 or 15,000 square meters.
Miki Naimi has built 140,000 of 350,000 square meters at Naimi Park near the Messubim Interchange and is developing another 140,000 square meters of offices.
Audicodes will move into Naimi Park in January after leasing 10,500 square meters; Sheba Medical Center Tel Hashomer leased 2,600 square meters and will grow to 5,300.
Newmark Natam's Or Ben Zvi Klein said small businesses moved from Ofakim and Sderot to Beer Sheva and Kiryat Gat on short contracts, and that property owners have not cut rents.

Ben Zvi Klein said owners who discounted early in Covid saw neighboring offices rent at NIS 140 per square meter versus a NIS 100 discount, and that owners rented most space in 2021-2022 peaks so they are not under pressure.
